title: Where Chapel Hill's New Condos and Townhomes Stand This Winter
summary: Coker Place, South Creek and 306 W. Franklin compared: prices, delivery dates, rent-first credits, and what September's Orange County inventory jump means for buyers.
body_markdown:
On Booth Park Boulevard, off North Estes Drive, a model townhome at Coker Place is open for self-guided tours. You don't need an appointment. The sales site advertises something new-construction buyers in Chapel Hill rarely see. On select homes, you can move in as a renter on a 12- or 24-month term, and 30% of each payment is credited to you if you buy. On the other side of town, across U.S. 15-501 from Southern Village, the developer of South Creek spent this summer advertising four months of free rent on 12-month leases at its first apartment building.


Both offers come from projects that are adding owned condos and townhomes to Chapel Hill. Both also come at a time when Orange County has more homes for sale than it did a year ago. A buyer comparing entry-level options in Chapel Hill this winter has time, and the new projects are competing for it.


## The county numbers behind the incentives


The most recent local figures come from the Durham Regional Association of REALTORS'[September 2026 market review for Orange County](https://durhamrealtors.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Combined-Entire-DRAR-Area-1.pdf) , which combines single-family homes, condos and townhomes. In September 2026, active inventory was 549 homes, 43.3% higher than in September 2025. New listings that month were up 42.2% from a year earlier, to 219.


Closed sales rose too, by 18.4% year over year to 116 in September. Sales grew more slowly than listings, though, and that gap shows up in months of supply. Orange County had 4.7 months of supply in September, up 21.1% from the year before. The median sale price for the month was $494,000, down 3.1% year over year, and sellers received a median 97.6% of list price.


Homes in Orange County still sold in a median 34 days in September, a pace that lets a buyer tour, compare and come back the following weekend. Builders have to price that patience into what they sell, and in Chapel Hill they are doing it with rent credits and lease concessions.


## Coker Place: the option you can move into now


Coker Place sits at 710 N. Estes Drive, next to Aura and Booth Park, close to UNC's Carolina North campus. Developer[Lock7](https://lock7.com/projects/710-n-estes) planned it as 40 townhomes and 67 condos, 14 of them affordable units. The project's sales site lists townhomes from the $600Ks and condos from the $300Ks. It has 18 floor plans, and some of them include private rooftop decks or personal elevators.


The townhomes came first. Lock7 had targeted December 2025 for the first move-ins. In its spring 2026 construction update, Coker Place reported that Buildings 1 and 9 were complete, that Building 1 was 30% sold, and that the first owners had closed that spring. The same update said Buildings 5 and 7, which have the first rooftop townhomes, were scheduled for the summer, and that construction on Building 4, the first condo building, would begin in early summer. The project's availability page now lists Buildings 1, 5, 7 and 9 as move-in-ready, and the condo plans are still marked as coming soon.


So the townhomes at Coker Place are finished homes you can walk through, priced above the county's September median. That pricing is where the Residency Credit comes in. The builder offers it on select homes, by application. A builder that offers it is giving buyers a year or two to decide while the home earns rent, and that works best when buyers are in no hurry. In practice, the credit turns part of a lease payment into a price reduction for a buyer who decides later.


## South Creek: the option you reserve for 2027


[South Creek](https://beechwoodhomes.com/south-creek) is much larger and further from move-in. The Beechwood Organization broke ground in September 2024 on land that had sat undeveloped for more than a decade as the stalled Obey Creek project.[Chapelboro reported at the groundbreaking](https://chapelboro.com/news/development/south-creek-development-breaks-ground-to-bring-800-new-homes-to-chapel-hill) that 80 acres would be kept as a nature preserve and park on one side of Obie Creek. In July,[The News & Observer](https://www.newsobserver.com/news/business/real-estate-news/article316457973.html) reported that the plan includes 606 condos, 100 townhomes and 92 apartments. About 15% of the condos and townhomes will be priced below market.


The condos are the first homes you can buy at South Creek. The N&O reported in July that pre-sales had opened on 68 condos starting at $325,000, with floor plans from studios up to three-bedroom homes as large as 2,234 square feet. Beechwood's South Creek page, updated in October, says condos are now selling from the high $300s and that first deliveries are expected in early 2027.[Chapelboro reported in March](https://chapelboro.com/news/development/chapel-hills-south-creek-neighborhood-celebrates-construction-milestone-announces-first-business-tenant) that the first condo building, the 68-unit Hawthorn, was targeting spring 2027, and that the 43-unit Weaver would follow.


The townhomes come later. Beechwood describes them as three-bedroom, 3.5-bath homes from 1,600 to 2,900 square feet, with rooftop terraces and garages, and lists their sales as opening in 2027. The 92 apartments at 95 Market Street are also scheduled to open in early 2027. Beechwood lists a coffee shop, an Italian restaurant and pizzeria, a cocktail lounge and Sounds & Colors Childcare Center among the neighborhood's businesses.


A South Creek buyer this winter is committing now to a home that won't be finished until 2027. In a tight market, that kind of commitment can secure a price before it rises. With 4.7 months of supply in Orange County this fall, the tradeoff runs the other way. You lock in a home and a building schedule, and you give up the option to buy whatever comes on the market in the meantime. If you are relocating for a job that starts in January, a spring 2027 condo means a lease in between. If South Creek's Southern Village side of town is the draw, our guide to[living in Southern Village](https://spotlightnc.com/blog/living-in-southern-village-chapel-hill) covers the established neighborhood across the highway.


## How the dates line up for a buyer this winter


Laid out by date, Chapel Hill's new for-sale supply looks like this:


1. Now: Coker Place's move-in-ready townhomes on Booth Park Boulevard, from the $600Ks, with the Residency Credit on select homes.
2. Early 2027: first South Creek condo deliveries, from the high $300s, along with the opening of the 95 Market Street apartments.
3. Later in 2027: South Creek townhome sales open.
4. Fall 2027: the target groundbreaking for 306 W. Franklin Street.


Coker Place's condos, from the $300Ks, are listed as coming soon without a published availability date.


The last project on that list was approved this month.[Chapelboro reported](https://chapelboro.com/news/local-government/chapel-hill-council-approves-updated-lumo-new-development-plan-for-306-w-franklin) that the Chapel Hill Town Council approved Redgate's seven-story plan for 306 W. Franklin 7–1 on November 18. The plan includes both apartments and condos, and the project now moves into design and financing.[Triangle Business Journal](https://www.bizjournals.com/triangle/news/2026/11/20/longfellow-life-sciences-scrapped-chapel-hill.html) put the total at 200 to 250 homes. If you want a condo on West Franklin Street, that one is years away. For this winter's decision, it matters only as a sign that more ownership options are on the way.


Seen together, the projects don't all arrive at once. Each one is at a different stage, and Coker Place, the only one with finished homes, is the one offering the most flexibility on timing. Meanwhile, the county's resale inventory was 43.3% larger in September than a year earlier. That means you can weigh a finished townhome near Aura, a condo reservation by Obie Creek and an existing resale home side by side, without being rushed by any of them.


## Questions buyers ask about Chapel Hill's new condos


**When can I move into a South Creek condo?** Beechwood lists first condo deliveries for early 2027. As of March, the first building, Hawthorn, was targeting spring 2027.


**Do the new projects include homes priced below market?** Yes. Lock7 lists 14 affordable units at Coker Place. At South Creek, 15% of the condos and townhomes will be priced below market, according to The News & Observer.


**Is the Residency Credit available on every Coker Place home?** No. The builder lists it on select homes, by application.


This post is general information, not financial advice, so confirm any purchase or lease terms with the right professional.
